resolution: Two Lean predicates carry the word, and the case never identifies them silently. `God` (DEF-GOD-AS-NAMED-IN-THE-SUMMA) is the bearer of the name in the Summa; STMT-MAXIME-ENS-IS-GOD is about it, and it rests on the open nominal premise STMT-GOD-NAMES-THE-UNIQUE-MAXIME-ENS, a reduced form of the q.13 a.8 ad 2 definition. `IsGod` (DEF-GOD-OF-CLASSICAL-THEISM) is the God of classical theism, used by STMT-GOD-EXISTS, stages 2-6 and the root; the step to it is the open identification premise STMT-UNIQUE-PURE-ACT-FIRST-MOVER-IS-GOD, in both stage-1 routes. ST I q.2 a.2 ad 2 licenses taking what the name signifies as the middle term of a proof from effects (DEF-NOMINAL-DEFINITION), so a nominal conclusion is the expected output of a way. 'What all understand by God' (q.2 a.3) reports usage and is a premise of no root-path result; the problem-of-evil signature has a third predicate, `Sig.God`, fixed by that usage as the first mover, so a consistency result there (POE-CATHOLIC-CONSISTENT-WITH-EVIL) is about that predicate, not about `IsGod`. A reviewer who finds 'God' in a conclusion must check which predicate the Lean theorem uses.
